What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient:
• Name: Not provided
• Age: 24-year-old
• Gender: Male

Hospitalization Dates:
• Admission: [not provided]
• Discharge: POD #20
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
• Patient underwent uncomplicated orthotopic liver transplantation after multiple thoracenteses for symtomatic relief of persistent right-sided hepatic hydrothorax.
• Patient presented with respiratory distress and left-sided infiltrates consistent with pneumonia on POD #5 after OLT. Patient was started on antibiotics and underwent a right-sided therapeutic thoracentesis with removal of 1.3 liters of fluid.
• Post-thoracentesis chest imaging revealed a large hydropneumothorax that was treated with a small-bore chest tube.
• Diagnostic bronchoscopy was not performed due to the absence of endobronchial obstruction on CT.
• Patient was stable without dyspnea and hypoxemia, so video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery was deferred after consultation with thoracic surgery.
• Patient was discharged home on POD #20 without supplemental oxygen.
• Follow-up chest x-ray 1 month later showed improvement in the hydropneumothorax and a chest x-ray obtained 6 months later showed near-complete re-expansion of the right lung without surgical intervention.

Discharge Instructions:
• Follow-up with liver transplant team as needed.
• Follow-up with primary care physician for ongoing care.

text:
The admission diagnosis was withheld, so this answer rests on an inference about the episode of care.

**Most likely principal diagnosis: J94.8 (Other specified pleural conditions), which covers hydropneumothorax.**

Reasoning:
- The summary describes the post-transplant course. The transplant itself was uncomplicated, and the indication (hepatic hydrothorax with underlying liver disease) is not stated in the summary.
- If the admission was for the transplant, the principal diagnosis would be the underlying liver disease, such as the cirrhosis that caused the hydrothorax. That condition isn't named, so I can't assign a code with confidence.
- Hepatic hydrothorax is coded K76.7 or K76.81 (hepatopulmonary syndrome is a separate condition), and in ICD-10-AM it is usually coded as J91* (pleural effusion in conditions classified elsewhere) alongside the liver disease code. It is a manifestation code and can't be the principal diagnosis.

**Suggested code set if the transplant admission is the episode:**
- Principal diagnosis: the underlying chronic liver disease (e.g., K74.6 Other and unspecified cirrhosis of liver), if documented.
- Additional diagnoses:
  - J91* Pleural effusion in conditions classified elsewhere (hepatic hydrothorax)
  - J94.8 Hydropneumothorax (iatrogenic, following thoracentesis, so J95.8 or J95.88 Other intraoperative and postprocedural complications of respiratory system may apply, with J93.8 for pneumothorax)
  - J18.9 Pneumonia, unspecified
  - Z94.4 Liver transplant status (not for the transplant admission itself)

**Answer:** Without the admission diagnosis, the best-supported single code is **K76.7/K74.6-type underlying liver disease** for a transplant admission. If the question is only about the clinical focus described in the hospital course, it is **J94.8 (hydropneumothorax)**, with J95.88 considered for a procedural complication.

Please provide the withheld admission diagnosis and I can give a definitive code.
